title: A Lion in a Banana-Leaf Hat: Meet the Mascot of Africa's First Olympics
summary:
Imagine a lion wearing a hat made of banana leaves. That's Ayo, the mascot of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games!

From October 31 to November 13, about 2,700 young athletes will gather in Senegal. They're all 17 or younger. They'll compete in sports like skateboarding, cycling, and baseball. The events happen in three places: Dakar, Diamniadio, and Saly.

Here's the big deal: this is the first Olympic Games ever held in Africa. Ever!

And the mascot has a cool story. Ayo the Lion was designed by Ndeye Mariama Diop, a 16-year-old from Senegal. Her lion wears a traditional Senegalese hat called a tingandé, made from banana leaves. Ndeye's design was picked from nearly 500 student entries.

"I was inspired by all the cultures of Senegal," Ndeye told Olympics.com.

So when the Games begin, watch for a smiling lion in a leafy hat — and remember, a teenager just like you helped create it.
why_it_matters: It reminds kids that big world events can happen anywhere, and that an idea from someone your age can end up being seen by millions of people.

background_read: Senegal (a country on the west coast of Africa) will host the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first time any Olympic Games have been held in Africa.
The Youth Olympic Games are a smaller Olympic event just for young athletes, with newer sports like skateboarding on the programme alongside older ones.
Every Olympic Games has a mascot, a friendly character that stands for the event and shows off something about the host country's culture.
